claims.claim_vi: The source describes five generators: UUID (128 bits, no service call, not sequential, poor for database indexing, collisions improbable), Snowflake (timestamp, machine ID, serial number, first bit unused, no network call, data-center id may be added), database auto-increment (transaction management guarantees uniqueness in one table, needs network, can expose business data such as user counts), database segment (batches cached in ID servers, saves I/O), and Redis key-value (in memory, faster than a database).
claims.verified_by: Source body read at the pinned commit.

claims.claim_vi: Toy run: 20000 inserts into a sorted list; random 128-bit values land before 5005.5 existing entries on average (19987 inserts not at the end); sequential values 0; time-ordered 64-bit values from two workers with random arrival inside the millisecond 0.25 (4998 inserts not at the end).
claims.verified_by: Run by the author on 2026-10-19 with a small Python program; counts only, no database benchmark. Program: brainstorm/system-design-101-vi/experiments/sd-11-028.py (asserts the recorded values).

claims.claim_vi: Birthday estimate for one billion random version-4 UUIDs (122 random bits) is about 9.4e-20; a segment allocator with batch 1 / 100 / 1000 makes 100000 / 1000 / 100 database calls for 100000 ids; a crash after 2500 ids of a 1000-batch leaves a gap of 500.
claims.verified_by: Computed by the author on 2026-10-19; RFC 4122 itself was not opened in this session. Program: brainstorm/system-design-101-vi/experiments/sd-11-028.py (asserts the recorded values).

design_notes_vi: Một khung năm thẻ cho năm cách sinh mã và một khung ghi chú kết quả thử chèn.
source_deviations: The source gives five short paragraphs; the lesson keeps the five generators and adds a four-question comparison table, an insertion-position experiment, a collision estimate and a segment-gap count, none of which are in the source.
The comparison table is the author's analysis, not a measurement.
Redis behaviour after a restart is the author's inference, not tested here.
